paragraphs.source_en: After making such a spectacle of myself, I felt somehow too ashamed to stay in the house and face Osan the maid. To change my mood, I slipped out of the kitchen to the back of the house, thinking I might as well go and visit Miss Calico, who lived at the house of the woman teacher of the two-stringed zither in the little lane. Miss Calico was a famous beauty in this neighborhood. I may be a cat, but I understand the tender sentiments well enough. At home, whenever I saw my master's sour face or was depressed by Osan's malicious treatment, I would visit this friend of the opposite sex; after chatting together, my spirits would lift before I knew it, and I would forget all my past worries and hardships, as though born anew. The influence of women is truly immense. Peering through a gap in the cedar hedge to see whether she was there, I found Miss Calico sitting properly on the veranda, wearing a new collar for the New Year. The roundness of her back was indescribably beautiful, the very perfection of curved grace. The curve of her tail, the way her legs were folded, and the elegant sight of her flicking her ears now and then with a touch of melancholy were beyond description. Especially as she sat there warmly and gracefully in the gentle sunlight, her posture solemn and composed, the fur all over her body, smoother than velvet, reflected the spring light and seemed to tremble softly even though there was no wind. For a good while I gazed at her in a trance; then, suddenly coming to myself, I called softly, "Miss Calico, Miss Calico!" At the same time I raised a forepaw and beckoned her over. Miss Calico at once said, "Oh my, it is you, sir!" She came down from the veranda, and the little bell fastened to her red collar jingled brightly. "To think they have even put a bell on you for the New Year; what an exquisitely clear sound." I could not help admiring it inwardly. Then Miss Calico came up beside me and said, "Sir, a happy New Year!" As she spoke, she waved her tail to the left. When we cats exchange greetings, we first stand our tails straight up and then swing them once around to the left. In this lane, Miss Calico is the only one willing to call me "sir." As I have already stated, I still have no name, but because I live in a teacher's house, Miss Calico alone treats me with respect and always calls me "sir." Naturally I rather enjoy being addressed that way, so I answered, "Yes, yes." "Yes, a happy New Year! You are splendidly dressed up today." I replied. Deliberately jingling the bell to show it off to me, she said, "Yes, my teacher bought it for me at the end of last year. Isn't it nice?" "It sounds splendid. In all my life I have never seen such a handsome bell." "Oh, really! Why, everyone wears one, doesn't she?" As she spoke she jingled it again for a while, then said, "Listen, isn't it a lovely sound? I am so happy!" When she had finished, she jingled it once more.
